title: Rustic Plum and Raspberry Tart
changes_from_base: Plums and raspberries in an open, hand-pleated pastry instead of a crème pâtissière tart.
summary: Sweet-tart plums and raspberries heaped in an open, pleated crust and baked until jammy.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
ice-cold water, plus 1 tbsp to glaze
ripe plums, halved, stoned and cut into 1 cm slices

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: blitz the flour and salt for 3 seconds. Scatter in the butter and pulse about 10 times, until crumbly, then tip into the bowl. Stop pulsing while you can still see flecks of butter.

steps.title: Hydrate
steps.text: stir in 90 ml of the cold water with the spatula, pressing until it clumps; add a little more only if needed. Shape a flat round, wrap and refrigerate 1 h (or up to 2 days).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: set the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and put baking paper on the tray. After 10 min at room temperature, roll the dough out to about 30 cm across and transfer it to the tray.

steps.title: Fruit
steps.text: mix the plum slices and raspberries with 60 g sugar, then heap them in the centre, keeping a 5 cm border clear.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: lift the border over the filling in loose pleats all the way round, leaving the middle open.

steps.title: Glaze and bake
steps.text: brush the folded edge with the 1 tbsp water and sprinkle with the remaining 15 g sugar. Bake 45-50 min, until well browned with bubbling juice.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: after 10 min, slide the tart off the paper onto the rack. Serve warm, about 30 min later. Warm slices hold together better than hot ones.

tips: Tart, dark-skinned plums give the best colour and flavour.
Add a spoon of extra sugar if your plums are very sour.
Serve with vanilla ice cream or plain yoghurt.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep loosely covered at room temperature for up to 1 day. Reheat in a 180 °C oven for 10 min to crisp the crust.
